title: Trump says Russia and Ukraine agreed to stop strikes on energy infrastructure
body:
On Sunday, 12 October 2026, US President Donald Trump announced a truce under which Russia and Ukraine would stop striking each other's energy infrastructure. On 13 October he said both sides had agreed and urged Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and Russian President Vladimir Putin to end the war. He said violations had occurred on both sides.

Zelensky said Russia hit at least six Ukrainian energy facilities after the truce was declared, and reported 33 people wounded on Monday. He said Kyiv supported an energy ceasefire, had not attacked Russian refineries and was ready to sign guarantees. Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov rejected any pause in fighting and said Russia would continue its special military operation.

Two days before the announcement, the United States had temporarily eased sanctions on Russian diesel, a decision criticised by Ukraine and Europe and questioned by lawmakers from both major US parties over whether it complied with US law. Al Jazeera noted that US midterm elections were due on 3 November, and that an AP-University of Chicago poll on 1 October found 65 percent of US adults blamed the White House for high living costs.
